questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: Pigment must be dispensed from the source bottle into a

answers.text: single-use ink cap placed on the procedure tray — never directly into the tube or machine
reusable glass palette that is disinfected between clients
cup of distilled water to dilute the pigment before use
the tube reservoir by dripping pigment directly from the bottle

explanations.a: Pigment must be dispensed from the source bottle into individual single-use ink caps placed on the procedure tray; the ink cap holds the pigment for that session only; dispensing into a dedicated ink cap prevents any needle-contaminated material from entering the source bottle, maintains the sterility of the remaining pigment supply, and provides a clear, accessible pool of pigment for the needle to pick up during tattooing.
explanations.b: Reusable glass palettes retain pigment residue in microscopic scratches and pores that cannot be fully cleaned and disinfected; they create cross-contamination risk between clients; single-use ink caps are the professional standard.
explanations.c: Diluting tattoo pigment with water is not standard procedure for most pigments; pigments are formulated ready to use or require specific dilution per manufacturer instructions; adding water before dispensing into an ink cap would not follow proper dispensing protocol.
explanations.d: Dripping pigment directly from the source bottle into the tube creates a direct contamination pathway — needle contact during tattooing can backflush contaminated material up the tube and into or toward the bottle cap, risking contamination of the source supply; pigment always goes into a separate ink cap first.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: When dispensing pigment from the source bottle to an ink cap, the bottle tip must

answers.text: touch the ink cap surface to ensure all pigment is transferred without waste
be wiped with the same glove used during tattooing to remove any residue
never contact the ink cap or any other surface in the procedure area — the bottle tip must remain clean to prevent contamination of the source supply
be pre-dipped in the ink cap to warm the pigment before dispensing

explanations.a: If the bottle tip contacts the ink cap, any contamination on or around the cap can be transferred to the bottle tip and subsequently into the remaining pigment supply; the bottle tip must remain free of contact with any procedure-area surface.
explanations.b: Wiping the bottle tip with a glove used during tattooing transfers blood and body fluid contamination from the glove to the bottle tip — and from there into the source supply; gloves used during a procedure are contaminated and must not contact source supply containers.
explanations.c: The pigment source bottle must be held above the ink cap and dispensed by tilting or squeezing without allowing the bottle tip to contact any surface in the procedure area; maintaining this no-contact protocol preserves the integrity of the remaining pigment for future sessions; the bottle tip must remain uncontaminated throughout the dispensing process.
explanations.d: Pre-dipping the bottle tip in the ink cap before dispensing creates direct contact between the tip and the potentially contaminated ink cap surface; this is a contamination event for the source supply and is never acceptable professional practice.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: Petroleum jelly (Vaseline) or tattoo ointment applied to the skin during the tattooing procedure serves to

answers.text: permanently seal the tattoo ink into the dermis once the needle deposits it
lubricate the skin surface to reduce needle friction, protect the stencil from premature removal, and keep the work area moist for better visibility of the tattoo during application
anesthetize the skin to eliminate pain during tattooing
act as an antiseptic barrier that sterilizes the skin between needle passes

explanations.a: Petroleum jelly does not seal ink into the dermis; pigment retention in tattooing is a biological process involving the dermis's response to the needle-deposited ink particles; an ointment on the skin surface has no effect on dermal pigment retention.
explanations.b: Petroleum jelly or specialized tattoo ointment is applied sparingly to the skin over the stencil area before tattooing begins; it lubricates the skin surface so the needle glides smoothly rather than dragging and catching on the skin — reducing skin trauma and discomfort; it also helps preserve the stencil by providing a barrier between the stencil ink and the rubbing action of wiping during tattooing; and it keeps the skin surface moist, making the tattoo lines more visible against the glistening skin as the artist works.
explanations.c: Petroleum jelly has no pharmacological anesthetic properties; it is a mechanical lubricant; topical anesthetics are specific formulations (containing lidocaine or other analgesics) that are separate products from petroleum jelly.
explanations.d: Petroleum jelly is not antiseptic; it is an occlusive petroleum-based emollient with no meaningful antimicrobial properties; it does not sterilize or disinfect the skin and should not be thought of as an infection control product.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: Tongue depressors used to dispense petroleum jelly from a shared container must be

answers.text: rinsed with water between dips to remove skin residue before returning to the container
shared between clients to reduce supply waste
soaked in the petroleum jelly container between uses during the same session
single-use — a fresh, unused tongue depressor is used each time product is dispensed; never double-dipped into the shared container

explanations.a: Rinsing and returning a used tongue depressor to the container is still double-dipping; rinsing does not remove microorganisms adequately; the contamination concern is the biological material from the client's skin that was picked up by the first dip — this cannot be reliably removed by rinsing with water.
explanations.b: Tongue depressors used to dispense from a shared container must never be shared between clients; using a depressor that has contacted one client's skin or blood in a container that will be used for future clients is a direct cross-contamination pathway.
explanations.c: Leaving the used tongue depressor soaking in the petroleum jelly container introduces contamination from the depressor (which has contacted skin) into the entire container supply; the petroleum jelly in the container would then be contaminated for all future uses.
explanations.d: Any implement used to dispense from a shared container must be single-use; a fresh, uncontaminated tongue depressor is used to remove the required amount of petroleum jelly from the container, and then that depressor is discarded — it is never returned to the container; this prevents client skin cells, blood, or microorganisms from the current client from entering the shared supply that will be used for future clients.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.2 — Demonstrates simulated procedure for tattoo application
questions.text: During the simulated tattoo application section, the power to the machine has been disconnected. This means the candidate demonstrates

answers.text: only the positioning of supplies without moving the machine at all
the correct hand position, machine angle, skin stretching, and procedural movements as if tattooing — without actual needle penetration of the skin
verbally describing the tattooing technique to the examiner instead of performing any movements
only the needle dipping motion into the ink cap without approaching the skin

explanations.a: The simulation requires the candidate to actively demonstrate tattooing technique movements — not simply arrange supplies in place; positioning alone does not fulfill the simulated procedure task.
explanations.b: With the machine power disconnected, the candidate demonstrates the full procedural technique — correct machine angle, hand position, skin stretching with the free hand, machine movement across the skin following the stencil — as if performing an actual tattoo; the absence of electrical power means the needle does not reciprocate, but the candidate mimics all movements and technique that would occur during live tattooing.
explanations.c: A verbal description alone does not demonstrate the physical competencies assessed in a practical examination; the candidate must perform the physical movements of the simulation.
explanations.d: Only demonstrating needle dipping would omit the critical assessment of machine handling, skin stretch technique, machine angle, and movement across the skin — all of which are evaluated during the simulated application section.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.2 — Demonstrates simulated procedure for tattoo application
questions.text: Stretching the skin taut during tattoo application is necessary because

answers.text: it prevents the client from feeling the needle by compressing the sensory nerves
it increases the surface area of the skin to accommodate larger tattoo designs
unstretched skin folds and bunches under the needle, producing uneven, jagged lines — a taut surface allows the needle to penetrate consistently at the correct depth and produce clean, even lines
it stimulates collagen production that improves tattoo healing outcomes

explanations.a: Skin stretching does not compress sensory nerves or reduce pain perception; it is a technique for achieving consistent needle penetration depth and clean line work — not a pain management technique.
explanations.b: Stretching does not permanently increase the skin's surface area; the skin returns to its natural state when tension is released; the purpose of stretching is technique-based, not a size accommodation.
explanations.c: Skin is an elastic organ that moves and bunches when a needle contacts it without tension; an unstretched skin surface undulates under the needle, causing the needle to penetrate at varying depths and angles, producing ragged, inconsistent lines; stretching the skin taut with the non-dominant hand (or a stretching grip) creates a flat, firm surface that allows the needle to penetrate consistently at the calibrated depth and track smoothly along the intended line — producing clean, precise work.
explanations.d: Skin stretching during tattooing has no documented effect on collagen production; wound healing is a biological process determined by the injury depth, immune response, and individual biology — not by surface tension applied during the tattooing itself.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.2 — Demonstrates simulated procedure for tattoo application
questions.text: The correct needle depth for tattooing implants ink into the

answers.text: stratum corneum (outermost epidermal layer) for maximum color retention
subcutaneous fat layer for permanent anchoring of the pigment
dermis — the layer between the epidermis and subcutaneous tissue — where pigment is encapsulated by fibroblasts and macrophages for long-term retention
epidermis only, where cellular turnover makes the tattoo gradually fade to a natural finish

explanations.a: The stratum corneum is the outermost, dead cell layer that sheds continuously through desquamation; pigment implanted only into this layer would be shed within weeks as the cells turn over — producing no lasting tattoo.
explanations.b: Implanting pigment into the subcutaneous fat layer places it too deeply; ink in the fat layer tends to spread through the loose adipose tissue, causing blurring, bleeding of lines, and a distorted appearance over time; it also causes unnecessary injury to the deeper tissue.
explanations.c: The dermis (specifically the papillary and upper reticular dermis) is the target layer for tattoo pigment; dermal cells (primarily fibroblasts) do not shed the way epidermal cells do; pigment particles deposited in the dermis are encapsulated by macrophages — some transported to lymph nodes, others remaining permanently encapsulated in the dermal tissue; this biological response produces the long-term retention of tattoo pigment.
explanations.d: The epidermis undergoes complete cellular renewal approximately every 28–40 days; any pigment implanted purely in the epidermis would be shed with the normal cell turnover and would not produce a lasting tattoo; tattooing must reach the dermis to be permanent.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.2 — Demonstrates simulated procedure for tattoo application
questions.text: The machine angle relative to the skin during tattooing primarily affects

answers.text: the electrical voltage consumed by the machine motor

the needle penetration angle, depth of pigment deposit, and resulting line quality — a near-perpendicular angle (75–90°) produces cleaner lines while shallower angles deposit pigment more superficially and may produce scratchy, inconsistent work
the amount of pigment held in the ink cap between needle dips
the speed of the machine motor's rotation

explanations.a: Machine angle does not affect voltage consumption; the power supply provides set voltage regardless of how the artist holds the machine.
explanations.b: The angle at which the tattoo machine is held relative to the skin surface directly determines: the angle at which the needle penetrates the skin (affecting which tissue layer receives the pigment); the effective depth of penetration for a given needle protrusion setting; and the quality of the resulting line — a near-perpendicular (75–90°) angle allows the needle to enter and exit the skin cleanly and consistently, depositing pigment in a controlled dot that, when repeated, creates clean solid lines; shallower angles cause the needle to enter the skin at a more grazing trajectory, depositing pigment inconsistently and potentially too superficially, resulting in scratchy, uneven, or patchy line work.
explanations.c: Ink in the ink cap is picked up by the needle tip through capillary action during dipping; the machine angle during tattooing does not affect ink cap volume.
explanations.d: Motor rotation speed is determined by the power supply voltage and machine design; the physical angle at which the artist holds the machine does not affect motor speed.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.3 — Adds additional ink cap and fills with ink
questions.keyword: adding ink cap and filling with ink
questions.text: When the examiner instructs the candidate to add another ink cap during the simulation, the new ink cap must be

answers.text: filled from the first ink cap's remaining pigment by pouring between caps
a new, unused cap filled with fresh pigment dispensed from the source bottle without the bottle tip contacting the cap
rinsed with the irrigation bottle before being filled with pigment
pre-filled from the candidate kit and placed on the tray before the examination begins

explanations.b: When adding an additional ink cap during the procedure, the new cap must be a fresh, previously unused cap; pigment is dispensed from the source bottle into the new cap using proper no-contact dispensing technique — holding the bottle tip above the cap without touching the cap, the procedure area, or any contaminated surface; this maintains the integrity of the source pigment supply while providing fresh pigment for the additional cap.
explanations.a: Pouring pigment from one used ink cap to another transfers any contamination present in the first cap (needle contact, skin cells) to the new cap and to the source pigment stream if any pigment flows back; caps must always be filled from the original bottle.
explanations.c: Rinsing with an irrigation bottle before filling introduces water into the cap, diluting the pigment and potentially interfering with the tattoo technique; ink caps are not rinsed before use.
explanations.d: Pre-filling ink caps before the examination begins is not the demonstrated technique; the examination assesses the candidate's ability to correctly dispense and add pigment during the procedure, not pre-set preparation before the session begins.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.3 — Adds additional ink cap and fills with ink
questions.keyword: adding ink cap and filling with ink
questions.text: Irrigation bottles used during tattooing must be

answers.text: filled with tap water at the studio sink immediately before each use
shared between multiple artists in a studio for efficiency
reused across multiple clients without any labeling requirements
labeled in English, contain appropriate liquid (distilled water or approved solution), and protected from contamination during the procedure with a barrier over the exterior

explanations.a: Tap water may contain microorganisms and minerals unsuitable for a clinical tattooing procedure; distilled water or sterile saline is preferred; additionally, the bottle must be labeled regardless of fill source.
explanations.b: Irrigation bottles must be individual-use for each client session; sharing bottles between artists creates cross-contamination pathways; each artist maintains their own labeled supply for each client.
explanations.c: Irrigation bottles in the NIC examination must be labeled in English; the CIB specifies 'Irrigation Bottles (Labeled in English)' in the suggested supplies list; proper labeling is required for all products.
explanations.d: Irrigation bottles at the NIC examination must be labeled in English; they should contain distilled water or an approved irrigation solution; the bottle exterior that is handled during the procedure must be covered with a barrier (plastic wrap or sleeve) to prevent blood and ink contamination from gloved hands from contaminating the bottle surface throughout the session; the barrier is changed between clients along with all other barriers.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.3 — Adds additional ink cap and fills with ink
questions.keyword: adding ink cap and filling with ink
questions.text: Between needle dips into the ink cap during tattooing, excess ink on the needle and tube tip is wiped with

answers.text: a single wipe cloth that is reused throughout the entire session to reduce waste
the back of the gloved hand to avoid using additional supplies
nothing — excess ink should remain to keep the needle lubricated
a clean paper towel or pre-moistened wipe designated for that purpose — fresh material is used throughout the session to maintain cleanliness of the work area

explanations.a: A single wipe cloth used repeatedly throughout a session accumulates blood, ink, and skin debris; wiping the needle on a cloth that already contains previous wipe residue recontaminates the needle tip with older, potentially more heavily loaded material; fresh wipe material should be used or the wiping cloth should be of sufficient size and folded to present clean areas consistently.
explanations.b: Wiping the needle on the back of the gloved hand contaminates the glove surface with ink and blood, which then contacts any other surface the gloved hand touches (machine, ink cap border, barriers); this spreads contamination throughout the work area.
explanations.c: Excess ink on the needle and tube tip obscures visibility, can drip onto the skin away from the work area, and creates an imprecise working environment; wiping is a standard procedural step.
explanations.d: During tattooing, the needle is periodically dipped into the ink cap to pick up pigment; between passes, excess ink on the tube tip is wiped using paper towels or designated wipe material kept within the barriered work area; fresh, clean material should be used to avoid accumulating large amounts of contaminated residue on a single cloth; the wipe material itself is considered contaminated waste and is discarded in the 'Trash' container at the end of the procedure.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.objective: 4.3 — Adds additional ink cap and fills with ink
questions.keyword: adding ink cap and filling with ink
questions.text: Why must the pigment source bottle be stored with its cap secured when not actively dispensing pigment?

answers.text: To prevent the pigment from evaporating, which would change its viscosity during the procedure
To comply with the NIC labeling requirement that original manufacturer caps must remain on all bottles

To protect the remaining pigment from airborne contamination in the procedure environment — blood aerosols, skin cells, and ink mist present in an active tattoo work area can settle into an open bottle and contaminate the entire remaining supply
To prevent the pigment from reacting with the oxygen in the air, which would permanently change its color

explanations.a: While viscosity changes can occur with excessive evaporation over time, this is a long-term storage concern; the primary reason for keeping the cap secured during a procedure is immediate contamination prevention from the active procedure environment.
explanations.b: Cap security is not specifically a labeling compliance issue; the manufacturer label requirement applies to the label on the bottle itself, not to cap closure during the procedure.
explanations.c: An active tattoo procedure generates fine aerosols of blood, ink, and skin debris from the reciprocating needle's action; these particles become airborne and can settle into any open container nearby; an uncapped pigment bottle in the procedure area is at risk of receiving these contaminated particles into the remaining pigment supply — potentially contaminating all future uses from that bottle; keeping the cap secured when not actively dispensing prevents environmental contamination of the source supply.
explanations.d: Standard tattoo pigment ingredients are formulated to be stable in contact with oxygen; the color stability concern with brief cap-off periods during dispensing is minimal compared to the contamination protection rationale; oxidative color change is a long-term storage concern, not a procedural cap-closure rationale.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: After the examiner instructs the candidate to conclude the tattoo procedure, the first step is to

answers.text: remove the machine from the client's arm and immediately disassemble the needle
apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly over the finished tattoo
stop the simulation, power off the machine (if connected), and begin the post-procedure wound care steps — cleaning the tattoo area and applying protective covering
ask the client to evaluate the tattoo and provide immediate feedback

explanations.a: Disassembly of the needle is a post-service cleanup step that occurs during the breakdown phase; immediate disassembly without first completing wound care would leave the client's skin unattended and skip required aftercare steps.
explanations.b: Petroleum jelly application is typically the final step after cleaning — not the first step in concluding the procedure; cleaning the skin of blood and ink residue comes before any protective application.
explanations.c: Upon instruction to conclude the tattoo procedure, the candidate stops the simulation, powers off the machine, and begins wound care: cleaning the completed tattoo area with an appropriate cleaning solution and clean materials to remove blood, ink, and lubricant; applying a protective covering (bandage, plastic wrap, or specialized tattoo covering as required by the jurisdiction) to protect the fresh wound from contamination; these steps complete the client's in-session care.
explanations.d: Client feedback and review of the finished work is a communication step that occurs after wound care is complete; while client approval is important, it is not the first procedural step in concluding the tattoo.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: Protective covering applied over a completed tattoo serves to

answers.text: enhance the visual appearance of the tattoo by keeping the colors vivid immediately after completion
protect the fresh open wound from environmental contamination and bacteria while allowing initial healing to begin, and to absorb any plasma and blood that weep from the fresh tattoo
permanently seal the ink into the dermis to prevent future fading
prevent the client from viewing the tattoo before paying for the service

explanations.a: A fresh tattoo covered by an opaque bandage cannot be seen; the covering's function is wound protection — not color enhancement; any apparent color vividness immediately after tattooing is from the fresh wound state, not the covering.
explanations.b: A freshly completed tattoo is an open wound — the needle has created thousands of punctures in the skin; the protective covering serves as a wound dressing: it protects the wound from environmental bacteria, dust, and pathogens that could cause infection; it absorbs the plasma, blood, and ink that weep from the fresh wound in the first hours; it provides a barrier against friction from clothing; and it creates a protected environment for the initial healing process to begin.
explanations.c: No topical covering can seal ink into the dermis; ink retention in the dermis is a biological process involving the encapsulation of pigment particles by fibroblasts and macrophages — a covering has no effect on this internal biological process.
explanations.d: The protective covering is a standard wound care step applied as part of professional responsibility for client wellbeing; it is not a commercial or payment-related measure.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: After-care instructions must be provided to the client at the conclusion of the tattoo procedure because

answers.text: state boards mandate that after-care instruction cards be submitted for regulatory review after each client
clients are required to sign a second consent form confirming they received instructions

the client's actions during the healing period directly determine the quality and longevity of the healed tattoo — improper after-care leads to infection, color loss, scarring, and the need for touch-ups
after-care products can only be purchased from the tattooist, so the client needs a product list

explanations.a: State boards may have record-keeping requirements but do not typically require submission of after-care instruction cards after each client; the primary reason for providing instructions is the client's healing outcome, not regulatory submission.
explanations.b: While a second signature confirming receipt of instructions may be part of some studios' documentation practices, the primary reason for providing after-care instructions is the clinical necessity of proper wound care during healing — not the signature itself.
explanations.c: A freshly tattooed area is an open wound that requires specific care during the 2–4 week healing process; the client must understand how to: clean the tattoo properly; apply appropriate moisturizers at the correct frequency; protect the healing tattoo from sun exposure, submersion in water, and picking or scratching; recognize signs of infection requiring medical attention; each of these behaviors directly affects whether the tattoo heals with vibrant, solid color or with fading, patchiness, or infection-related complications.
explanations.d: After-care products are widely available; the reason for providing after-care instructions is clinical — proper wound healing — not commercial product sales.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: The reason the needle must not be removed from the tube while the machine is powered on is

answers.text: removing a powered needle creates a risk of accidental needle penetration of the artist's gloved hand or a bystander from the rapidly reciprocating needle
the machine will be permanently damaged if the needle is removed while power is on
powering off is required by state board regulations before any maintenance
the tube becomes too hot to handle when the machine is running

explanations.a: When the machine is powered on, the needle reciprocates at high speed (hundreds to thousands of times per minute depending on machine type and voltage); attempting to remove or adjust the needle while it is in motion creates a significant needlestick injury risk — the rapidly moving needle can easily penetrate a gloved hand, cause an uncontrolled sharp movement, or create a splash of blood-contaminated material; the machine must be powered off and the needle must be stationary before any assembly or disassembly is performed.
explanations.b: While powered operation during disassembly is not designed use and could cause mechanical wear, the primary concern is the needlestick injury risk to the artist — not equipment damage.
explanations.c: While regulatory compliance is relevant, the specific operational safety reason is the needlestick injury risk; state board regulations on this topic exist because of the underlying safety hazard.
explanations.d: Standard tattoo machines produce some heat from motor operation, but the tube does not become dangerously hot to handle; the needle reciprocation injury risk is the operative safety concern, not tube temperature.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: Blood-contaminated paper towels and wipe material used during the tattooing procedure must be placed in the container labeled

answers.text: 'Trash'
'To be Disinfected/Sterilized'
'Sharps'
the candidate supply kit for transport as biohazardous waste

explanations.a: Blood-contaminated soft waste items (paper towels, wipe material, gauze, used ink caps, stencil backing) that are not sharps and are not reusable implements are discarded in the 'Trash' container; in a professional studio, blood-contaminated soft waste may be regulated as biohazardous waste depending on jurisdiction and quantity; for the NIC examination, these items go in the 'Trash' container rather than the 'Sharps' or 'To be Disinfected/Sterilized' containers.
explanations.b: The 'To be Disinfected/Sterilized' container is for reusable implements; single-use soft waste items are not reusable and cannot be reprocessed.
explanations.c: The 'Sharps' container is for items that can puncture or lacerate — used needles, blades, lancets; soft, non-piercing paper towels and wipe material do not belong in a sharps container.
explanations.d: Contaminated waste materials must not be placed in the supply kit; the kit is for clean supply storage; the NIC examination requires all contaminated waste to go into the appropriate labeled waste containers at the point of use.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: After the examiner instructs the candidate to stop the simulation and conclude, the model is excused when

answers.text: the candidate completes the disposal of all contaminated supplies at the end of Section 4
the machine has been powered off and the clip cord disconnected
the candidate raises their hand to indicate the entire examination is finished
the examiner has completed their assessment of Section 4 and reads the instruction that the model is excused

explanations.a: Completing supply disposal occurs during Section 5 (Breakdown); the model excusal is a specific examiner instruction that occurs at the end of the examiner's Section 4 assessment — before the Section 5 breakdown begins.
explanations.b: Powering off and disconnecting the clip cord are procedural steps within the section; they do not trigger the model's excusal; the excusal is an examiner-initiated instruction.
explanations.c: The candidate raising their hand indicates section completion; the model's excusal is specifically triggered by the examiner's verbal instruction after completing their assessment — not by the candidate's hand raise.
explanations.d: The NIC CIB specifies that after the examiner has completed their assessment of Section 4, the proctor reads: 'The examiner has indicated they are ready to proceed. The model is excused at this time.' — this examiner-triggered verbal instruction is what officially excuses the model; this sequence ensures the examiner has fully evaluated the conclusion steps before the model leaves the examination area.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: The used needle, after being removed from the machine at the conclusion of the procedure, must be

answers.text: recapped using a two-handed technique and placed in the 'To be Disinfected/Sterilized' container
dropped directly into the 'Sharps' container without recapping, bending, or breaking
wiped with an EPA-registered disinfectant wipe before disposal to reduce contamination in the sharps container
immediately dropped into the 'Trash' container since it is a single-use item

explanations.a: Two-handed recapping is explicitly prohibited by OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard as a primary needlestick injury prevention measure; additionally, used needles belong in the 'Sharps' container — not in the 'To be Disinfected/Sterilized' container, which is for reusable implements.
explanations.b: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard requires that contaminated needles not be bent, broken, recapped using two hands, or otherwise manipulated by hand; they must be dropped directly into an OSHA-approved sharps container at the point of use; the container must be close enough to the work area to allow immediate disposal without carrying the uncapped needle through the space.
explanations.c: Wiping a used needle with a disinfectant wipe before disposal requires handling the sharp, blood-contaminated needle — creating unnecessary needlestick risk; the needle goes directly into the sharps container without additional processing.
explanations.d: Used needles are sharps and must go in the 'Sharps' container — not the 'Trash' container; placing sharps in the trash creates needlestick hazards for anyone handling the waste bag after disposal.

questions.name: Simulated Tattoo Procedure and Conclusion
questions.text: Blood exposure during the tattoo procedure — if the artist's glove is punctured by the needle — requires which immediate response?

answers.text: Continue the procedure and address the puncture at the end of the session to avoid disrupting the client
Apply topical antibiotic ointment to the puncture site and continue working with double gloves

Stop the procedure, remove and discard the punctured gloves, wash hands thoroughly, re-glove, assess the exposure, and follow the studio's or examination's blood exposure protocol — including reporting the incident
Soak the gloved hand in the irrigation bottle solution for 2 minutes before continuing

explanations.a: Continuing to work after a needlestick or glove puncture prolongs exposure to blood and prevents proper immediate wound care and incident documentation; the procedure must stop immediately.
explanations.b: Topical antibiotic ointment is a minor wound care step but does not address bloodborne pathogen exposure protocol; simply double-gloving does not clean the puncture wound or initiate the required post-exposure response; the full exposure protocol must be followed.
explanations.c: A glove puncture during tattooing is a potential bloodborne pathogen exposure incident; the immediate response follows OSHA's post-exposure protocol: stop the procedure; remove the compromised gloves immediately using proper technique; wash the exposure site thoroughly with soap and water (or irrigate mucous membranes); re-glove and assess the wound; report the incident to a supervisor or examiner; seek medical evaluation promptly (within hours) for post-exposure prophylaxis assessment; document the incident per OSHA and facility requirements; the NIC CIB explicitly states candidates will be expected to follow proper blood exposure procedures.
explanations.d: Immersing the gloved hand in irrigation solution does not address the glove puncture or bloodborne pathogen exposure; the fluid in an irrigation bottle is typically distilled water, not a disinfectant, and would not adequately address the exposure; proper handwashing of the exposed skin is required.
